info.title: matter-bridge MQTT API
info.description:
Everything matter-bridge publishes and accepts on MQTT.

Topics here use the default base topic, `matter` (`mqtt.base_topic` in the configuration), and Home Assistant's default discovery prefix, `homeassistant` (`homeassistant.discovery_prefix`). `{device}` is the name a person gave a device, given at commissioning or with `rename` (`node_<node id>` otherwise). Clusters, attributes, commands and events are named in `snake_case` from the Matter data model, or by id in hex where the data model does not know them; requests take a name or a number.

The bridge publishes and subscribes at QoS 1. Payloads are JSON unless a message says otherwise. Requests go to `matter/bridge/request/<name>`; the answer comes on `matter/bridge/response/<name>`, echoing the request's `transaction` so a client can match the two. Fabric keys, Check-In keys and network credentials never appear on MQTT.

unique_id.description:

`matter_<compressed fabric id>_<node id>_<endpoint>_<cluster>`.

object_id.description: The entity id Home Assistant derives: `<device>_<endpoint>_<cluster>`.

availability.description: The bridge's and the device's availability topics.

availability_mode.description: `all`: the entity is available while both are.

state_topic.description: The attribute topic the state is read from.

value_template.description: Picks the state out of the attribute's value.

state_value_template.description: Lights: turns the on/off attribute into `ON` or `OFF`.

command_topic.description: Lights and switches: the endpoint's `on_off/set` topic.

state_on.description: Switches: the state that means on.

state_off.description: Switches: the state that means off.

brightness_value_template.description: Dimmable lights: reads the level, 0 while it is null.

payload.description:
A Home Assistant MQTT discovery config, retained on
`<discovery_prefix>/<component>/<device key>/<endpoint>_<cluster>/config`:
one entity per light, switch, sensor or battery. An empty retained
message removes the entity. Keys are Home Assistant's; see its MQTT
integration's documentation.
payload.title: DiscoveryConfig

payload.description:
A new value for an attribute, on
`<device>/<endpoint>/<cluster>/<attribute>/set`, as JSON in the same
form the attribute is published in. An enumeration may be given by name.
payload.title: AttributeWrite

payload.description:
A value for an on/off or level control endpoint, on
`<device>/<endpoint>/on_off/set` (`ON`, `OFF`, `TOGGLE`, or `true` and
`false`) or `<device>/<endpoint>/level_control/set` (a level, 0 to 254,
switching the light on). Plain text or JSON.
payload.title: ClusterSet

payload.description:
A command's fields, on `<device>/<endpoint>/<cluster>/command/<command>`:
an object keyed by the data model's field names, or an empty message for
a command without fields. A required field that may be null can be left
out.
payload.title: CommandFields

code.description:
The QR code's payload (`MT:...`) or the manual pairing code,
with or without dashes.

name.description:
The device's name; `node_<node id>` if left out. It must not be
`bridge`, or contain `/`, `#` or `+`.

address.description: The device's address as `ip:port`, to skip discovery.

timeout.description:
Seconds to look for the device; `matter.discovery_timeout` if
left out.

wifi.description:
For a Wi-Fi device reached over Bluetooth: the network to give
it. Never stored or logged.

thread_dataset.description:
For a Thread device reached over Bluetooth: the network's active
operational dataset, as hex. Never stored or logged.

thread_dataset_url.description:
Where to read the Thread dataset instead: an OpenThread border
router's REST API, e.g.
`http://127.0.0.1:8081/node/dataset/active`. Without either,
`matter.thread_dataset_url` is used.

transaction.description:
Any value; the response echoes it, so a client can match the
two.

oneOf.description: Looking for the device, over DNS-SD or Bluetooth LE.

Checking the device's attestation.
Asking the device for its operational key.

OtaStep.description:
A step of a software update, as the bridge sees it. The device's own OTA
Software Update Requestor events tell the download's progress.

oneOf.description: The device asked for an update and was offered `version`.
The device downloaded it and was told to apply it.
The device reports it now runs `version`.

manufacturer.description: The vendor's name, from Basic Information.

DiscoveryDevice.description: The device an entity belongs to, in Home Assistant's device registry.

value_template.description: Picks `online` or `offline` out of the payload, for `bridge/state`.

DiscoveryAvailability.description: An availability topic Home Assistant watches.

password.description: Its passphrase; empty or left out for an open network.

WiFiCredentials.description: A Wi-Fi network to give a device.

manual_code.description: The pairing code to enter in the other app, `XXXX-XXX-XXXX`.

qr_code.description: The same as a QR code payload (`MT:...`).

discriminator.description: The discriminator the device advertises while the window is open.

Id.description:
A cluster, attribute or command: its `snake_case` name from the data
model (any case, with or without underscores), or its id as a number.

anyOf.description: The name, or the id as `0x` hex or decimal text.

cluster.description: The cluster's name, or its id in hex.

attribute.description: The attribute's name, or its id in hex.

value.description: Its value, `null` when `status` says why there is none.

status.description:
The status the device gave instead of a value, such as
`UnsupportedAttribute`; `null` for a value.

Commissionable.description: A device that can be commissioned, seen over DNS-SD.

vendor_id.description: The vendor it is for; 0 for any.

product_id.description: The product it is for; 0 for any.

min_applicable_version.description: The oldest version it applies on top of.

max_applicable_version.description: The newest version it applies on top of.

OtaImage.description: A Matter OTA image file in `matter.ota_dir`.
